answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a public randomness beacon — a lantern that publishes an unpredictable seed every epoch. Before an agent may transact, it must compute a verifiable delay function over that seed plus its own identity kernel, a proof that takes real, non-parallelizable time. Identities also grow along a trellis of mutual attestations from established peers, so a new fake must pay compute for every epoch and still starts with no trust. An attacker creating ten thousand Sybils pays ten thousand delay proofs per epoch, while an honest agent pays one.
